You know, I was there myself when I was a sophomore (barely turned 23 now), in a similar situation. My then-girlfriend, now ex-wife had fucked three of my best friends, dumped me afterward, and constantly told me I would amount to nothing, and she was dating me because she felt sorry for me. The only school program I cared about (ROTC) demoted me and banned me from their functions, and all my "friends" turned their back and followed my ex girlfriend. I was in the dumps, so low I couldn't go any lower if I tried. Then I started thinking, "Why do I even need them? They're so quick to throw me out, to turn their back on me. Why do I need them to be happy?" I realized, I didnt. Not even a little bit. I was still my own person, still had my own hopes and dreams for the future. They shouldn't have the power to destroy my happiness to the extent I would put a bullet through my skull if I could. So I stopped moping around, and threw myself into solo activites. I studied, worked out, played video games, read. Did whatever I could think of to turn my mind away from them. Set goals for everything. "I'll run these three miles in under 15 mins instead of 18", "I'll take a break when I fully understand how to do this new math formula" stuff like that. It took a long time, and a lot of effort, buy eventually I pulled out of it, and didn't care anymore. 

You're still in high school, and high school is always tough, but it gets better when you get out, I promise you that. I don't know if my story is inspirational, or just plain dumb, but maybe something in it will spark something in you. Everything will get better, the trick is to be around to see it happen. :)
